He calls for the Law Commission and Parliament to explore giving the SRA the powers it needs to effectively regulate lawyers. 

Without such powers, how can misconduct by lawyers be uncovered?

Giving expert evidence to the committee, Rupert Cowper-Coles from RPC LLP responds that while legal privilege is a fundamental right, if the regulator does not have the powers to access client-lawyer communications under any circumstances, then, “bad conduct is going to flourish”.

Chair of the Justice Committee, @catherineatkinson.bsky.social asks whether parliament should legislate so that the Solicitors Regulation Authority can access confidential communications between a lawyer & their client in order to investigate alleged professional misconduct.
